title: Safe iframe and sandbox concepts
learningObjectives: Explain safe iframe and sandbox concepts and apply safe browser programming practices.

understand.concept: An iframe embeds another browsing context. The sandbox attribute restricts capabilities such as scripts, forms, popups, and same-origin access unless specific permissions are granted. Permissions Policy and a restrictive Content Security Policy can add further controls. Avoid granting more capabilities than needed.
understand.whyItMatters: Embedded content may be untrusted or independently controlled. A sandbox is a defence-in-depth boundary, but combinations such as allow-scripts with allow-same-origin can weaken isolation for same-origin content.
understand.analogy: An iframe sandbox is like a room with selected doors locked; each permission opens a specific capability.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; browser APIs, security boundaries, and accessibility requirements are defined by web platform standards.

explain.narrative: The iframe has an empty sandbox attribute, so scripts and other capabilities are restricted by default. Add tokens only when a requirement is understood.

examples.explanation: The iframe has an empty sandbox attribute, so scripts and other capabilities are restricted by default. Add tokens only when a requirement is understood.
examples.expectedOutput: The example demonstrates the API or security principle; browser permission or environment support may be required.

practise.guidedTask: Create a static sandboxed preview. List which capabilities each sandbox token grants and explain why untrusted learner code must not access the parent app.
practise.independentTask: Build a small browser feature using the API or safety principle. Test normal, denied, unavailable, and invalid cases where relevant.
hints: Treat data from the browser, URL, and network as untrusted.
Ask permission only after explaining the purpose.
Keep sensitive authorization and secrets on a trusted backend.

questions.prompt: What does an iframe's sandbox attribute do by default?
options: Restricts capabilities of the embedded browsing context
questions.answer: Restricts capabilities of the embedded browsing context
questions.explanation: An empty sandbox attribute applies a restrictive set of browsing-context restrictions.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable approach for browser-facing features?
options: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
Assume every browser grants every permission
questions.answer: Use least privilege, clear user feedback, and appropriate server checks
questions.explanation: Browser features should respect user choice, validate inputs, and enforce protected actions on the server.
